properties.name: exchange.auth.authority-host
properties.description: Authority host, overridable for sovereign/government clouds (e.g. "https://login.microsoftonline.us/" for US Gov, "https://login.partner.microsoftonline.cn/" for the 21Vianet China cloud). The tenant id is appended to this to form the full authority URL - never hardcode the public cloud value if your organization operates in a sovereign cloud.

properties.name: exchange.auth.cache-enabled
properties.description: Whether acquired tokens are cached in-memory to avoid hitting Entra's token endpoint on every call. Defaults to true.

properties.name: exchange.auth.cache.expiry-buffer-seconds
properties.description: How many seconds before a token's ACTUAL expiry it's proactively treated as expired and refreshed. Protects against a token expiring mid-flight on a slow downstream call, or clock skew between this service and Entra ID. Default 300s (5 minutes).

properties.name: exchange.auth.cache.max-size
properties.description: Maximum distinct cache entries (one per distinct scope-set, or per distinct OBO caller+scope-set).

properties.name: exchange.auth.certificate.alias
properties.description: Alias of the entry to use. If omitted, the keystore's first alias is used.

properties.name: exchange.auth.certificate.path
properties.description: Filesystem path to the PKCS12 keystore.

properties.name: exchange.auth.client-secret
properties.description: App Registration client secret. Set this OR {@link #certificate}'s path, not both. A certificate is the stronger, recommended credential for anything handling real data - see that nested class's Javadoc.

properties.name: exchange.auth.connect-timeout-millis
properties.description: HTTP connect timeout for calls MSAL4J/the JWKS fetcher make to Entra ID, in milliseconds.

properties.name: exchange.auth.read-timeout-millis
properties.description: HTTP read timeout for the same calls, in milliseconds.

properties.name: exchange.auth.scopes
properties.description: Default scopes requested for the Client Credentials flow, e.g. "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default".

properties.name: exchange.auth.tenant-id
properties.description: Azure/Entra Tenant ID (GUID or verified domain, e.g. "contoso.onmicrosoft.com"). Required.

properties.name: exchange.auth.validation.expected-audience
properties.description: Expected `aud` claim - typically your own app's client id (for tokens issued TO your app) or a resource identifier (e.g. "https://graph.microsoft.com" for tokens meant to call Graph). Left blank, audience is not checked - acceptable for a quick start, but set this explicitly for anything handling real data: without it, validateToken() only proves "signed by this tenant", not "intended for this application".

properties.name: management.endpoint.exchange-auth.access
properties.description: Permitted level of access for the exchangeAuth endpoint.

properties.name: management.endpoint.exchange-auth.cache.time-to-live
properties.description: Maximum time that a response can be cached.

properties.name: management.endpoint.exchange-auth.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable the exchangeAuth endpoint.
